findings.summary: B2's human recovery exit is not exposed through the MCP control surface. DdControlPlane.recover() is implemented but build_mcp_server registers no corresponding tool, and SUPPORTED_TOOLS contains only the eight pre-existing tools; tests/test_dd_service.py:153-171 asserts that set exhaustively, pinning the omission. No CLI path reaches recover() either, so the spec's 'expose a deliberate human recovery exit through the MCP control surface' is unmet.

B2 adoption is neither automatic nor reachable. AdoptionLedger.discover() has no caller in src/, and DdControlPlane.adopt() has no caller and no MCP or CLI surface, so no discovery path folds eligible in-flight/recoverable work into the governed workflow. The spec requires adoption on discovery 'rather than requiring a manual bookkeeping intervention'; what exists is a manual entry point nothing can invoke. (The idempotency-by-signature property itself is correctly implemented.)

B3's mandated 'suspended-to-resumed MCP human-recovery case' is absent. tests/test_human_recovery.py exercises the in-memory HumanRecoveryExit with a stubbed authenticate lambda, never the MCP surface; DdControlPlane.recover() and DdControlPlane.adopt() have no test coverage at all, leaving the board-decision authentication and the file-backed idempotent replay of the adoptions/recoveries jsonl trails unexercised.

The B3 evidence chain is a parallel structure not bound to the real artifact/receipt/event trail. fleet_graph/dd/evidence.py is imported by nothing in src/ -- the control plane's own evidence() assembly does not use EvidenceChain -- and in the chain the test builds, each link's mechanism and evidence_mechanism are the same string literal typed twice, so the 'substituted an unrelated event' check is satisfied by construction rather than by asserting that the artifact was produced by the mechanism the test identified.

B1's boundary is enforced only against spec text at admission, not against handoffs. require_scope is called from exactly one site, DdControlPlane.create, over the spec bytes; no dispatch, handoff, or stage-artifact path is scope-checked. The spec requires rejecting or quarantining work crossing the boundary 'including references or handoffs that attempt to add B4 or revive katana#150/katana#151'.

The committed implement handoff records work_head_commit as 7fa6ee88161ed80de41a73f1100146c91ced76e3, while the attempt context supplied to this review names the product commit (work_head_commit) as 62eaacb5ec2f0cc4bc17f6979eec9f3321f91307. The two disagree; one of the two records is stale or mislabeled.

B1-B3-SPEC.md at the repository root is a byte-for-byte duplicate of .dev-dispatch/spec/approved.md committed into the product tree. Whether this change introduced it could not be determined without git history; if it did, the frozen digest-bound copy under .dev-dispatch/ is the single source and the root duplicate invites divergence.

The mandated product-consistency check (git diff --exit-code between the implement and review subject commits, excluding .dev-dispatch) was not executed: this reviewer role has file-inspection tools only and shell access was declined. No claim is made about its exit status, and no finding is raised on that basis; the review was conducted against the worktree contents at /data/worktrees/fleet-graph-b1-b3-20260828.
